passages.provision_quote: A firearm industry member shall not advertise, market, or arrange for placement of an advertising or marketing communication concerning any firearm-related product in a manner that is designed, intended, or reasonably appears to be attractive to minors.
passages.note: The operative section regulates firearm marketing to minors, a dimension this ladder does not order.

rows.reasoning: The only record is Lackey's No on AB 2571 (2021-2022), whose operative section says "A firearm industry member shall not advertise, market, or arrange for placement of an advertising or marketing communication concerning any firearm-related product in a manner that is designed, intended, or reasonably appears to be attractive to minors." An advertising rule does not say which firearms may be owned, bought or carried, so it cannot reach "Allow all types of firearms, but require universal background checks on every sale" or any other rung; per the annex, a No on such a bill is no more on-question than a Yea. Nothing else survives, so the row is blank for want of evidence.
needs_source: Lackey's own words, or a California Assembly roll call on a bill that sets which firearms may be owned, bought or carried (assault-weapons scope, universal background checks on private sales, or carry permits)
